pages.title: Sun - Dunks + Sprints A (One Foot, Lateral)
pages.body:
SUN - DUNKS + SPRINTS A
One-foot takeoff, lateral landings, long hill sprints. This is the harder of the two jump days and it runs on the freshest legs of the week, straight off Saturday.
Wednesday is the two-foot vertical day. Do not mix them.
LAST SUNDAY ___ | top height made ___ ft | attempts used ___ | bound ___ in | box ___ in | sprints ___
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week: 8 dunk attempts, half the landing block, 2 sprints. Same intent, half the contacts.

PREP - continuous, no rest - 7 min
Short Foot Holds - 2x20s ea
Tibialis Raises - 2x15
Banded Ankle Inversion/Eversion - 2x12 ea
Hip Internal Rotation Lift-Offs - 2x8 ea
Adductor Squeeze - 2x20s
Glute Bridges - 2x12
Then 3 min easy court movement, A-skips and lateral shuffle.

LANDING AND DECELERATION - rest 45s - 8 min
This goes before the dunks, not after. It is 30 sticks, it does not tire you out, and it primes the exact landing you are about to do 16 more times. It is also the only sideways single-leg landing work in your week, so it does not get skipped.
Lateral Bound to Stick - 3x3 ea (new)
Depth Drop to Single-Leg Stick, 12 in box - 2x3 ea (new)
Stick every landing a full 2 seconds, silent, knee tracking out over the middle toe, second foot never touches. If it wobbles, shorten the bound or lower the box. Do not accept a sloppy rep.

ONE-FOOT RAMP - rest 60-90s
1 up 2 down - 2x3 ea leg
3 to 4 step run-in, drive the opposite knee hard, land on two and absorb. Max height every rep. This is the ramp into the dunks, not a conditioning set.

DUNK PROGRESSION, ONE FOOT - HARD CAP 16 ATTEMPTS TOTAL - rest 60-90s, 2 min once the rim is high
Count every attempt. At 16 the block is over even if you were making them.
Get loose, 9 ft rim, two-foot takeoff - 3 attempts
Off-foot approach, rim touches only - 3 attempts
1-foot 2-hands at 9.5 ft, strong takeoff foot - 4 attempts
Raise 2 in, strong foot - 3 attempts per height until you fail a height
1-foot off a live gather, one dribble into the takeoff - 3 attempts at your best made height
Off foot stays submaximal for the first 6 weeks: rim touches and clean approaches only, no dunk attempts and no rim raises on that foot until you can touch the same height off both feet.
Three misses in a row at any height ends the block. Do not grind dunks.

HILL SPRINTS - rest 2:30, the slow controlled walk down is the rest
Hill Sprints - 4x40 yd, full sprint, drive the first 10 yards, do not decelerate before the line
Rep 4 should look like rep 1. If rep 3 is visibly slower, stop at 3 and take 3:00 rest next week.

FLUSH - no rest
Easy flat walk - 5 min
Tibialis Raises - 1x20

STOP RULES
Two flat or slow attempts in a row ends that block, whatever is left on the page.
Any knee or ankle pain on a landing ends all jumping for the day. Do the sprints, skip the rest.
Rest periods are not negotiable. When time runs short you cut attempts, never rest.
Game week or a travel week: this day stays, Wednesday's jump day is the one that drops.

PROGRESSION
There is no barbell today, so height and distance are your load. Overwrite the LAST SUNDAY line at the top of this page every week or you are not progressing them.
Lateral Bound to Stick: progress by DISTANCE only, never reps. Stick all 9 reps clean each side, then add about 6 in to the bound next Sunday. Sets and reps stay 3x3 ea forever. This is the only place this movement lives and the only rule it has.
Depth Drop to Single-Leg Stick: when all 6 reps each side stick silent and motionless for 2 seconds, raise the box 2 in. Cap 20 in. Hold 12 in for the first 6 weeks regardless.
1 up 2 down: stays 2x3 ea leg. Progress is jump height, not reps.
Dunk Progression: log the highest height you converted and how. Next Sunday start 0.5 ft below it. Only attempt a brand new height on a day you hit last week's height on the first try. When you make a height on the FIRST attempt on two separate Sundays, that height becomes your new starting height.
Hill Sprints: stay at 4 forever. Progress is the same 4 sprints getting faster, not a 5th sprint.
Bad day rule: if the first lateral bound lands heavy, cut the landing block to 2x3 ea, cap dunks at 8, and still do the sprints. Never make up missed jump volume later in the week.

pages.title: Mon - Heavy Lower
pages.body:
MON - HEAVY LOWER
Court day done. Practice tomorrow at 4:00. The purpose is max force, then leave. Never grind here.
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week, date written on the NEXT DELOAD line in advance: same lifts, same sets and reps, 85 percent of your written weights.

TODAY IS A OR B - check the LAST RUN line
LAST RUN: ___ (A or B)   date ___          NEXT DELOAD: week of ___
It says A, today is B. It says B, today is A. First time through, today is A.
A missed Monday never advances the letter. Skip a week and you pick up exactly where you left off.
Overwrite the LAST RUN line with today's letter and date before you touch a bar.

PREP - 1 set each, minimal rest - 6 min
Short Foot Hold - 1x20s ea
Tibialis Raises - 1x15
Banded Ankle Inversion/Eversion - 1x12 ea
Hip Internal Rotation Lift-Offs - 1x8 ea
Glute Bridges - 1x12

POWER - WEEK A ONLY - rest 2 min
Ramp: empty bar 1x5, then 50 percent 1x3, then 70 percent 1x2
Power Cleans - 3x3 ___ lb
Week B skips this block entirely. Cleans never share a day with heavy deadlifts.
Bar speed is the metric. The moment a rep slows, the set is over, even with reps left.

MAX FORCE - rest 3-5 min, full rest, no rushing
Ramp the HEAVY lift only: 40 percent 1x5, 60 percent 1x3, 75 percent 1x2, 85 percent 1x1. Ramp rest 60-90s. All percentages are off today's top work set, not off an all-time max.
The LIGHT lift gets one ramp set only: 60 percent 1x3.
Run one block below, never both. Only one of these two lifts is heavy on any given Monday.

WEEK A - BACK SQUAT HEAVY
Back Squat - 4x3 ___ lb
Deadlift - 2x5 ___ lb

WEEK B - DEADLIFT HEAVY
Deadlift - 3x3 ___ lb
Back Squat - 2x5 ___ lb

Back squat is the lift the team tests you on, so it is the lift that owns the main slot.
The light lift is 60-65 percent of that lift's current heavy triple. Fast off the floor, groove it, stop early if it drags.
Leave one rep in the tank on every heavy set. You have practice in under 24 hours.

POSTERIOR AND SINGLE LEG - rest 2 min
Nordic Hamstring Curls - 3x5
Bulgarian Split Squat - 3x5 ea ___ lb

FINISHER - rest 90s
Sled Push - 3 down-and-backs ___ lb
Suitcase Carry - 2x40 yd ea ___ lb (new)
Carry tall, zero side lean, free arm hangs dead and does not counterbalance.

PROGRESSION
A set with no weight written next to it did not happen. The weight in the blank IS the record - overwrite it when it goes up.
Clean set = every prescribed rep, last rep moves as fast as the first, no grind, no back rounding, no touch from a spotter.
Back Squat and Deadlift: all heavy sets clean, add 10 lb the next time that lift is HEAVY. Count sessions you actually did, never weeks on a calendar - a missed Monday changes nothing except when the next one lands. Any set slow or grindy, run the same weight again. Same weight stalls twice in a row, drop it 10 percent and build back.
The light lift is always 60-65 percent of that lift's current heavy number, so it climbs on its own. Never add to it on purpose.
Power Cleans: add 5 lb only when all 9 reps were fast and none had to be muscled up. One slow rep, repeat the weight.
Nordic Hamstring Curls: no load. Earn reps, 3x5 to 3x6 to 3x7 to 3x8, and only once you control the full descent with hips locked out. If your hamstrings are still sore on Tuesday morning, run 2x5 for two weeks before going back to 3x5.
Bulgarian Split Squat: add 5 lb per hand when both legs get all 5 clean reps for all 3 sets. The weaker leg sets the weight for both.
Sled Push: add 10 lb when all 3 down-and-backs hold the same pace unbroken. Same rule as Friday's reverse sled.
Suitcase Carry: add 5-10 lb when both 40 yd trips are zero side lean and the grip never slips.
Deload: if Back Squat and Deadlift both stall across two heavy sessions each, take 20 percent off both for one week, then restart the ladder.
IN-SEASON, from Sep 1: this day does not change. It is the anchor. If a week has two games, Friday drops to ATG squat, Cossack squat and the sled only.

pages.title: Tue - Upper System
pages.body:
TUE - UPPER SYSTEM
Practice is 4:00-5:50 PM. Train this in the morning gym block, six hours clear of practice.
Nothing goes to failure today. Hardest set stops at 7 out of 10. If a set gets ugly, the set is over. Position is the whole point of this day.
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week: drop one set from every exercise on this page.

T-SPINE AND SCAP PREP - no rest, flow through it
Quadruped T-Spine Rotations - 2x8 ea
Serratus Wall Slides - 2x10
Serratus Wall Hold - 2x15s

SYSTEM PRESS - rest 90s - pick a bell you own for all 3 sets
Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press - 3x8 ea ___ lb
Wrist stacked, ribs down, no lean. The bell wobbling is the exercise failing, not the exercise working.

ROTATE AND RESIST - rest 60-75s - alternate all three
Half-Kneeling Landmine Rotations - 3x8 ea ___ lb
Half-Kneeling Pallof Press - 3x8 ea, 2s hold at full extension ___ lb (new)
Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row - 3x10 ___ lb (new)
One block trains rotating, one trains refusing to rotate, one is your second rowing exposure of the week. Chest supported means zero low-back cost before practice.

CARRIES - rest 60s - rack and overhead only, no farmer grip before practice
Front-Rack Kettlebell Carry - 2x40 yd ___ lb (new)
Single-Arm Overhead Carry - 2x20 yd ea ___ lb (new)
Ribs down under the rack. Overhead arm stays locked with the biceps by the ear, no rib flare.

BRACED CORE - rest 45-60s - hips square, ribs down
Bridge Russian Twist - 2x10 ea ___ lb
Kettlebell Pull Through - 2x8 ea ___ lb

SHOULDER HEALTH - rest 45s
Side-Lying External Rotations - 3x12 ea ___ lb

No log table for this day on purpose - the weight in the blank IS the record here. Overwrite it when it goes up.

PROGRESSION
Write a weight in every blank every week. No number, no progress.
Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press: hit 3x8 on both arms with zero wobble and no wrist collapse, then go up one bell next Tuesday and restart at 3x5, building back to 3x8.
Half-Kneeling Landmine Rotations, Bridge Russian Twist, Kettlebell Pull Through, Side-Lying ER: hit all sets and all reps clean two SESSIONS in a row, then add 5 lb. Miss reps or lose position, repeat the same weight. Never drop weight.
Half-Kneeling Pallof Press: hold the full 2 seconds on every rep with hips and ribs dead still, then add one plate or one band level. If your ribs flare or you rotate at all, the weight is wrong.
Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row: all 3 sets of 10 controlled with a 1 second squeeze at the top and no torso movement, then go up one dumbbell.
Carries: cover the full distance with no lean and no shoulder sag, then go up one bell. Set it down early, repeat that weight. Distance stays fixed, load is what moves.
Hard cap: nothing on this page goes above 7 out of 10. If a jump makes a set feel like a max, you added too soon, go back one step. You have two hours of practice this afternoon and this session is not allowed to cost you anything there.

pages.title: Wed - Dunks + Sprints B (Two Foot, Vertical)
pages.body:
WED - DUNKS + SPRINTS B
Two-foot takeoff. Vertical and bilateral. Short accelerations instead of long hills.
You had practice yesterday at 4:00, so this day is deliberately the easier of the two jump days. Sunday is the one-foot lateral day and it stays on the fresh legs.
LAST WEDNESDAY ___ | top height made ___ ft | attempts used ___ | sprints ___
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week: 10 dunk attempts, skip the depth drops, 3 sprints.

PREP - continuous, no rest - 6 min
Short Foot Holds - 2x20s ea
Tibialis Raises - 2x15
Banded Ankle Inversion/Eversion - 2x12 ea
Hip Internal Rotation Lift-Offs - 2x8 ea
Deep Bodyweight Squats - 2x10
Then 3 min easy jog and court movement.

STRAIGHT-AHEAD BRAKING - rest 45s
Single-Leg Snapdown to Stick - 3x3 ea (new)
Fast drop to a quarter squat on one leg, dead stop, second foot never touches, hold 2 seconds. Straight ahead only today. Sideways landings are Sunday.

TENDON STIFFNESS - rest 60s
Pogo Jumps - 3x10
Ankles only, knees nearly straight, silent and instant off the floor. This is a bouncing set, not a jumping-high set. Cut the set the moment a contact goes long or loud.

VERTICAL POTENTIATOR - rest 2 min, full rest between every set
Depth Drop into Box Jump - 2x3, drop box ___ in, jump box ___ in
Step off the box, do not jump off it. Absorb and go straight back up with no pause on the floor. Walk back and reset between every rep. This is 6 reps to switch you on before the rim, not a training block of its own.

DUNK PROGRESSION, TWO FOOT - HARD CAP 20 ATTEMPTS TOTAL - rest 60-90s, 2 min once the rim is high
Count every attempt. At 20 the block is over even if you were making them.
Get loose on a 9 ft rim - 4 attempts
Left-right two-foot - 3 attempts
Right-left two-foot - 3 attempts
Two hands, left approach - 3 attempts
One hand, right approach - 3 attempts
Raise to 9.5 ft, best approach - 4 attempts
Keep raising 2 in per round inside the cap. Highest height converted today ___ ft, how ___
Three misses in a row at any height ends the block. Do not grind dunks.

HILL SPRINTS, SHORT ACCELERATIONS - walk down slow, rest to 2:00
Hill Sprints - 5x15-20 yd on the steepest section, staggered 2-point start, alternate lead foot
Sunday is the long 40s. Today is pure acceleration. The first 6 steps are the whole rep.

COOL DOWN - 3 min
Easy walk - 3 min
Ankle, knee and hip CARS - 2 slow reps each direction, counts toward tonight's set

STOP RULES
Two flat or slow attempts in a row ends that block, whatever is left on the page.
Any knee or ankle pain on a landing ends all jumping for the day. Do the sprints, skip the rest.
If yesterday's practice cooked your legs, cut to 12 dunk attempts and 3 sprints and skip the depth drops. Cut volume, never intent.
Game week or a travel week: this is the jump day that drops. Sunday stays.

PROGRESSION
No external load is added on this day. Progress here is height and speed only, never more reps and never a vest.
Pogo Jumps: stay at 3x10. When all 30 contacts are silent and instant two weeks running, go to 4x10 and stop there. Never add reps past 10.
Depth Drop into Box Jump: stays 2x3. When you land all 6 reps silent with no foot adjustment and rebound straight back up, raise the DROP box 2 in. Cap the drop box at 24 in. Raise the JUMP box 2 in only when you clear it with daylight on all 6 reps.
Single-Leg Snapdown to Stick: stays 3x3 ea. Progress the speed of the drop, not the reps. When every rep is a dead stop with zero second-foot touch for two weeks, drop from a 4 in box instead of from standing.
Dunk Progression: when you make a height on your FIRST attempt on two separate Wednesdays, that height becomes your new starting height and you raise the rim 2 in.
Hill Sprints: when all 5 reps feel the same speed two Wednesdays running, add a 6th. Cap 6 reps, then use a steeper hill instead of adding reps.
Overwrite the LAST WEDNESDAY line at the top of this page every week. The box heights and the height converted are already blanks on this page - overwrite those too.

pages.title: Thu - Heavy Upper
pages.body:
THU - HEAVY UPPER
Heavy day. Write a weight in every blank. Nothing goes to failure today.
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week: same lifts, same sets and reps, 85 percent of your written weights.

PREP - rest 45s
Scap Pull-Ups - 2x8
Dead Hang - 2x25s
Band Pull-Aparts - 2x15 ___ band (new)

BENCH RAMP - rest 60-90s
Empty Bar - 1x10
Ramp 1 - 1x5 at 50 percent of today's work weight ___ lb
Ramp 2 - 1x3 at 70 percent ___ lb
Ramp 3 - 1x2 at 85 percent ___ lb
Ramp 4 - 1x1 at 92 percent, fast and clean ___ lb

MAX FORCE PRESS - rest 3-4 min, full rest, no rushing
Bench Press - 5x3 ___ lb
Low reps, real weight, real rest. This is the upper half of your max force output, so treat the rest periods as part of the lift.

HEAVY PULL - alternate the two, rest 90s after every set, stop 2 reps short on every set
Weighted Pullups - 4x4 ___ lb
Barbell Row - 4x6 ___ lb (new)
The row is the fix for having had no horizontal pulling at all. Torso locked, bar touches the same spot every rep. Your second rowing exposure is Tuesday.

GRIP AND WRIST - rest 45s
Grip Hold - 2x20s ___ lb
Wrist Extension Iso - 2x15s
Wrist Flexion Iso - 2x15s

PROGRESSION
If the weight is not written in the blank, the set did not happen. The weight in the blank IS the record - overwrite it when it goes up.
Bench Press: work weight is one you could take for 5 clean triples with 2 reps still in the tank on the last set. No max known yet, use a weight you can press for 6 clean reps and run your triples with that. When all 5 triples move fast with no grind, add 5 lb next Thursday. Miss a rep or grind badly, repeat the same weight. Two stalled weeks in a row, drop 10 percent and build back.
Weighted Pullups: all 4 sets of 4 clean, chin over bar, no kip, and 2 still left on the last set. Then add 5 lb. If set 4 drops below 4 clean reps, keep the same weight next week.
Barbell Row: all 4 sets of 6 with the torso locked in place and the bar touching the same spot every rep. Then add 5 lb. If your back is swinging to move the bar, the weight is wrong, drop 10 lb and earn it back.
Band Pull-Aparts: when 2x15 finishes with the band touching the chest every rep and no shrug, go up one band level. Write the band colour in the blank.
Grip Hold: when both 20s holds are easy, add weight, never add time.
Wrist isos: bodyweight, no load. Progress by holding a harder angle, not longer.

pages.title: Fri - Lower Lengthened
pages.body:
FRI - LOWER LENGTHENED
Loaded end range. Nothing here is a stretch. Every rep is you owning range under load.
Write the weight in every blank, every week.
DELOAD WEEK, every 4th week: drop one set from every exercise on this page.

PREP - flow straight through, no rest
Tibialis Raises - 2x15
Hip Internal Rotation Lift-Offs - 2x8 ea
Adductor Squeeze - 2x20s
Deep Bodyweight Squats - 2x10

LOADED END RANGE - rest 2 min, alternate the two
ATG Squat - 3x6 ___ lb - 2s pause in the hole, heel flat
Cossack Squat - 3x6 ea ___ lb - sit all the way down, straight-leg heel stays down, no hand support

HINGE AND POSTERIOR AT LENGTH - rest 90s
Kettlebell Swing - 3x8 ___ lb
Jefferson Curl - 3x8 ___ lb - one vertebra at a time, no bounce, no speed

ANTERIOR CHAIN AT LENGTH - rest 60s
Reverse Nordic - 3x8 - control down AND up
Hip Flexor Iso Raise - 2x15s ea

CALVES - rest 60s
Seated Calf Raise - 3x12 ___ lb - 3s pause at the bottom stretch
Standing Single-Leg Calf Raise - 3x8 ea ___ lb (new) - knee dead straight, full stretch at the bottom, 2s pause at the top
The seated version is bent knee and only trains soleus. The standing straight-knee version is the Achilles tendon and gastroc, which take every landing you make on Sunday and Wednesday and had no heavy slow load anywhere in the week until now.

TENDON ISO - rest 45s
Spanish Squat Hold - 2x30s ___ lb

FINISHER - rest 60s
Reverse Sled Drag - 3 down-and-backs ___ lb

STOP RULE - read this one
Any central low-back ache that is still there the next morning, or any pain on single-leg standing back-bend, means Jefferson Curls and heavy Deadlifts both come out of the program until it has been looked at. That is not negotiable and it is not a bad week, it is a signal.

No log table for this day on purpose - the weight in the blank IS the record here. Overwrite it when it goes up.

PROGRESSION - read before you load anything
Log the weight in every blank every week. No log, no progression.
Add weight on at most two lifts per week. End range gets earned slowly.
ATG Squat: add 5 lb when all 3 sets hit 6 reps with the heel flat and no bounce out of the bottom. If any set loses depth, same weight next week.
Cossack Squat: add 5 lb when both sides hit 6 full-depth reps, straight-leg heel down, no hand support.
Jefferson Curl: add 2.5 to 5 lb only after two straight SESSIONS of clean 3x8. Maximum 5 lb added per month. HARD CAP 25 lb for your entire first training block regardless of how easy it feels. After the cap, progress tempo and segmental control, not load. This is the one lift where the rule can outrun the tissue with no warning.
Kettlebell Swing: next bell up when all 3x8 float to chest height on hip drive alone, no arm pull.
Seated Calf Raise: add 10 lb when 3x12 holds the 3s bottom pause and a 1s squeeze at the top.
Standing Single-Leg Calf Raise: add 5 lb per hand when both legs hit 3x8 through full range with a dead-straight knee and a real 2s pause. The weaker side sets the weight.
Reverse Nordic: progress RANGE, not weight. Hands on thighs, then arms crossed, then arms overhead. Move up only when 3x8 is controlled in both directions.
Reverse Sled Drag: add 10 lb when all 3 trips are unbroken at the same pace. Same rule as Monday's sled push.
Holds: add 5 seconds when the last set looks like the first. Cap Spanish Squat Hold at 45s, then add load in the blank instead of adding time.
Hard rule: if the position breaks, the weight does not go up. You never buy range with weight.

pages.title: Sat - Mobility
pages.body:
SAT - MOBILITY
LAST RUN: ___ (A, B or C)   date ___
It says A, today is B. It says B, today is C. It says C, today is A. First time through, today is A.
A missed Saturday does not advance the letter - you pick up where you left off.
Overwrite the LAST RUN line with today's letter before you start. Never count Saturdays on a calendar.
DELOAD WEEK: this day is unchanged. It is the one day that never gets cut.

THE POINT OF TODAY
Passive range is range something else could push you into. Active range is range you can hold with nothing but your own muscle.
The gap between those two is uncontrolled range. No strength in it, no control in it. That gap is where ankles roll, hamstrings tear and shoulders get angry.
Nothing today is a stretch. Every rep is you contracting at the end of your own range until that range belongs to you.
CARS map the range. PAILs/RAILs push the end of it further out. Lift-off holds close the gap behind it.
This is the same practice you already do every morning and every night, slowed down with ten times the attention.

FULL CARS SWEEP - all 11 joints, every week - no rest, keep moving - 12 min
One rep is 20-25 seconds. Slow, maximum tension, keep breathing. If it is fast it is not a CARS.
Toe CARS - 1 ea direction ea foot
Ankle CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Knee CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Hip CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Trunk and Spine CARS - 1 ea direction
Scapular CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Shoulder CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Elbow CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Wrist CARS - 1 ea direction ea side
Finger CARS - 1 ea direction ea hand
Neck CARS - 1 ea direction

HOW EVERY PAILs/RAILs SET RUNS - same for every joint - rest 60s between joints
This block is second on purpose. It is the only part of the day that actually expands range, so it happens while you are fresh and it never gets cut.
Get there - move to your own end range under your own power. No bouncing, nobody pushing you.
Push in - PAIL. Press INTO the barrier. Ramp from 20 percent up to 70 percent effort over 10s, then hold 15s. Keep breathing.
Pull deeper - RAIL. Without moving an inch, switch to contracting the muscles that would drag you further into the range. Same ramp, hold 15s. This is the half people skip and the half that works.
Sink - relax 5s, then actively move a little deeper. Under your own power only.
Repeat - 2 rounds per side, then one 10s unsupported hold at the new end range.
Two joints a Saturday plus the small ones. Two done honestly beats ten done fast.

WEEK A - HIPS AND ANKLES - cutting and landing - 18 min
Hip Internal Rotation PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Ankle Dorsiflexion PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Toe and Finger End-Range Iso - 2x15s ea (new)

WEEK B - T-SPINE AND OVERHEAD - shooting and posture - 18 min
Thoracic Rotation and Extension PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Shoulder Flexion and Scapular Upward Rotation PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Wrist and Elbow End-Range Iso - 2x15s ea (new)

WEEK C - HINGE AND SHOULDER ER - posterior chain and arm care - 18 min
Hip Flexion and Extension PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Shoulder External Rotation PAILs/RAILs - 2 rounds ea (new)
Neck and Knee End-Range Iso - 2x15s ea (new)

ACTIVE RANGE HOLDS - every week, this is the gap closer - rest 30s - 11 min
No hands, no support, nothing to lean on. If you shake, that is exactly the point.
Hip Internal Rotation Lift-Off Hold - 2x10s ea
Hip External Rotation Lift-Off Hold - 2x10s ea (new)
Kneeling Dorsiflexion Active Hold - 2x15s ea (new)
Quadruped T-Spine Rotation Lift-Off - 2x5 ea with a 5s hold (new)
Prone Overhead Lift-Off Hold - 2x15s (new)
Prone 90/90 External Rotation Lift-Off - 2x10s ea (new)

OWN THE RANGE - finish here - no rest - 5 min
Range you open and never use is gone by Tuesday. Go use it.
Deep Squat Sit with slow reach and rotation - 2x30s
Slow Split Squat, 5s down, 3s pause, 5s up - 1x5 ea
90/90 Hip Switch, no hands - 1x10 total (new)

PROGRESSION
Write two things next to every hold, on this page: seconds held clean, and whether you shook or cramped. No number, no progress.
Active-range holds: hold the prescribed time twice in a row with zero shake and zero support, then add 5s. At 30s stop adding time and make the position harder instead - longer lever, less support, or a 2 to 5 lb plate in the hand or on the foot.
PAILs/RAILs: before you start a joint, find your unsupported active end range and mark it against something fixed in the room. Beat last cycle's mark and that joint is progressing - then add 5s to the isometrics or a third round.
Small-joint end-range isos: add 5s when the last set looks like the first, cap at 30s.
If a joint has not moved in two full A-B-C cycles, stop calling it a mobility problem. It is a strength problem. Take that exact position to Monday or Friday and load it.
Cramping during a RAIL means the range is new. Keep going. Sharp joint pain is not that - back off about 10 percent of the range and rebuild.
Never chase passive range. The only number that counts is range you can hold on your own.

pages.title: Rules - Missed Days + Testing
pages.body:
RULES - MISSED DAYS, TESTING, DELOAD
Read this once. It covers what to do when the week does not go to plan, which is most weeks.

IF YOU MISS A DAY
Never double up. A missed session is gone. Trying to make it up costs more than it returns.
When the week gets cut short, this is the order of what matters:
1. Mon Heavy Lower and Thu Heavy Upper - these are why you lift at all. Protect these first.
2. Sat Mobility - the cheapest day you have and the one that keeps you available.
3. Fri Lower Lengthened - injury insurance.
4. Sun and Wed jumps - two is a ceiling, not a target. One is fine. Zero for a week is fine.
5. Tue Upper System - the first thing to drop.

SLIDING A HEAVY DAY
You can move a heavy day one day forward if you land on a jump day or on Tuesday.
Never move a heavy day onto the day before practice.
Never run two heavy days back to back.

THE LETTERS TAKE CARE OF THEMSELVES
Miss a Monday and you do NOT skip a letter. The LAST RUN line on the Monday page still says
whatever it said, so the next Monday reads it and carries on. Same for Saturday's A/B/C.
Only ever overwrite a LAST RUN line on a day you actually did.

MISSED TWO OR MORE DAYS IN A WEEK
Run the deload numbers on whatever is left instead of cramming. A short easy week beats a
crammed one, and it costs you nothing over a season.

MISSED A JUMP DAY
It is gone. Never make up jump volume later in the week. Jumping tired is how you get hurt
and it does not make you jump higher.

LOGGING A MISSED DAY
Never write a letter for a day you did not do. The LAST RUN lines are what the A/B and A/B/C
rotations read, so a letter means "I ran this session".
A missed day is simply not written. The next real session reads LAST RUN and picks the letter up
where you left off.
Every progression rule in this program counts SESSIONS YOU DID, not weeks on a calendar.
Miss three Mondays and your next Monday is simply the next one - nothing resets, nothing is owed.

TEAM TESTING DAY - MAX SQUAT, BENCH, CLEAN
Testing IS your session that day. Do not add anything to it. It is already a max force day,
just programmed by someone else.
Log it here, on this page:
TEAM TEST: date 2026-08-31   squat 335 lb   bench 285 lb   clean 205 lb   (your text to Dad that night; next test week of 10/15)
That week only:
- Thursday: skip the bench, keep the barbell row and the weighted pullups. You already maxed
  the press this week and your shoulders do not need a second one.
- Wednesday: drop the jump day if your legs are flat. Sunday's stays.
- Tuesday: unchanged. It is already capped at 7 out of 10 and you have practice that afternoon.
- Friday: unchanged, but go by feel on the ATG squat load.
Your letter does not advance on a testing week.
The upside: once you have real maxes, every percentage in this program stops being a guess.
Bring the three numbers back and the ramps and working weights get filled in properly.

DELOAD - EVERY 4TH WEEK
Mon and Thu: same lifts, same sets and reps, 85 percent of your written weights.
Tue and Fri: drop one set from every exercise.
Sun and Wed: half the contacts, same intent.
Sat: unchanged. It is the one day that never gets cut.

pages.title: GOOD DRILLS - How they work
pages.body:
GOOD DRILLS - HOW THEY WORK
Read once. This page is the rule for every Good page in the library.

WHAT A GOOD DRILL IS
A Good drill is not a shooting drill or a finishing drill. The shot at the end is the outcome,
not the point. The point is the mess before it.
You are training three things and only these three:
  PERCEPTION - how little time you need to see it and decide
  BALANCE - producing force from positions you should not be able to produce force from
  PACE - doing both of the above at game speed instead of workout speed
GOOD DRILLS APPLY TO SKILLS, NOT SITUATIONS. Handling, shooting, finishing - things you
execute. Off ball, ball screens and team defense are positioning and decisions, not skills, and
they belong in the reps rotation and at practice instead.

DRILLS ARE COMPOUND, NOT ONE CONCEPT AT A TIME
A good drill pays several bills in one rep. Crawl start, spin, spin back, touch the backboard,
adjust and finish on the way down is off-balance AND max height AND an air adjustment AND almost
no time to see the rim - four targets, one rep. Build them that way. A drill that trains exactly
one thing is usually a drill that could have trained three.

WHY THERE ARE NO MAKE STANDARDS ON THESE PAGES
Because the way you hit a make standard on a deliberately awkward rep is by making it less
awkward. Shorter fall, earlier gather, straighter entry, easier angle. A make count on a Good
drill quietly pays you to delete the drill.
Bag pages have make standards. 50/50 has a make standard. Good pages do not. Different job.

HOW YOU PROGRESS - THE LEVEL, NOT THE MAKES
Every Good page runs at a LEVEL. The level is how uncomfortable the setting is. You move up when
you can hold the QUALITY at the current level, not when you make more shots.

L1  Clean entry. Learn the shape of the drill.
L2  Awkward entry - fall start, crawl start, spin start, off-balance, on the move already
L3  Less time - the ball arrives late, you go before you are set, no gather you did not earn
L4  Full pace - sprint into everything, no walking between reps
L5  Late decision - the cue comes as late as you can make it come
L6  Tired - run it after conditioning or at the end of the block, not fresh
L7  Two at once - stack any two of L2 to L6

THE QUALITY TEST - this is what you are judging, every rep
Did you finish the rep balanced enough to do something else immediately after it?
If you land, stumble, and reset, the level is too high. If you never feel the edge, it is too low.
You want to be on the edge of losing it and not losing it. That is the whole training effect.

MOVING UP
Hold the quality for two sessions at a level, go up. Lose the quality twice, go back down.
Write the level on the NOW line next to the drill. There is no shame in L2 forever on the hardest drill on the page -
levels are per DRILL, not per page. Some of your drills will sit at L5 and some at L2 and that
is the system working, not the system failing.

WHAT TO FILM
Once a month, film one drill from each Good page at your current level. You cannot feel your own
balance and you cannot feel your own pace. You can see both.

pages.title: Good Finishing
pages.body:
GOOD FINISHING
Compound drills. No make standards except X layups. Scale by LEVEL, not by makes.
Write your level next to each drill. Move it when you own it, drop it when you do not.
Two Good Handles drills come first, before this page. Some drills here also enter through
handling - see the entries menu below.

HANDLING ENTRIES - the menu. Any drill below can be entered through one of these.
Higher levels on every ladder call for one. This is where handling in awkward situations and
sharpening moves live now - they are how you ARRIVE, not a separate workout.
  CHASE IT       throw it ahead off the wall or a hard roll, sprint it down, pick it up moving
  SCRAMBLE UP    start on the floor with the ball already bouncing, get to your feet, go
  OUT OF THE BOX two chairs a body width apart, work it low and fast, explode out
  TWO BALL DROP  two going, drop one, immediately go with the other
  OFF A COUNTER  killer cross to burnsey, in and out to spin, reverse through to euro,
                 misdirection through and behind, lowmans
THE SHARPNESS TEST: did the move take you somewhere? Alone, a move that ends where it started
was decoration. Ground covered is the measure.

YOUR FOUR TARGETS AND WHERE THEY GET HIT
                              glass height | perception | air adjust | spots+hands
Crawl Spin Touch Finish            core         core         core         some
Fall Start Menu                    some         some         some         core
Crawl Into Touch                   -            core         some         some
Loose Ball Finish                  -            core         some         core
Every session runs 2 or 3 of these. All four targets get hit either way.

1. CRAWL SPIN TOUCH FINISH                                    NOW: L___
Crawl start, spin, spin back, jump and touch as high as you can, adjust in the air, finish on
the way down.
Off balance from the spins, max height on the glass, an adjustment mid-air, and almost no time to
see the rim because you are already coming down. Four targets, one rep.
  L1  Crawl start, one spin, touch the NET, finish. Strong hand.
  L2  Touch the rim instead of the net
  L3  Touch the backboard
  L4  Add the spin back
  L5  Both hands
  L6  Get up later off the crawl - less time before you have to go
  L7  Finish is called AT the touch, not before it
  L8  Off arm pinned to your side - no balance arm
  L9  Land on one foot, hold it two seconds
  L10 Enter it off a handling entry
  Start at whatever height you can actually reach. Touching the net cleanly beats missing the
  backboard. The touch is the hardest part of this drill and there is no shame in climbing it.

2. FALL START MENU                                            NOW: L___
3/4 court fall start, through through through, into a finish off the menu.
Touch backboard | Reverse | Free throw extension | Same foot same hand high | Pinoy slow |
Free throw float | 1 foot change feet and hands
  L1  Walk-in speed, fixed finish, strong hand
  L2  Full speed
  L3  Both hands, every finish
  L4  Finish called at the free throw line
  L5  Finish called at the block
  L6  Full court instead of 3/4
  L7  Off arm pinned to your side
  L8  Enter it off a handling entry
  L9  Land on one, hold

3. CRAWL INTO TOUCH                                           NOW: L___
Crawl start into a fade or a float. Soft hands off a bad position.
  L1  Crawl into fade, strong hand
  L2  Crawl into float
  L3  Both hands on both
  L4  Get up later
  L5  Which one is called as you rise
  L6  Off one foot
  L7  Off hand holding a second ball
  L8  Enter it off a handling entry

4. LOOSE BALL FINISH                                          NOW: L___
Roll it out or off the wall, chase it down, pick it up, finish from wherever you got it.
  L1  Slow roll, strong hand, any finish
  L2  Faster roll
  L3  Roll it to your weak side
  L4  Pick it up going backwards
  L5  Bad bounce off the wall instead of a roll
  L6  Finish called as you pick it up
  L7  From a dive to your feet
  L8  Off a counter into the finish - burnsey, spin layup, euro

X LAYUPS - 2/2 or it doesnt count. No level, no scaling.
Same foot same hand | Euro | Wide down the lane | Pinoy
Your clean reference - the version with nothing wrong with it, so you know the finish itself is
sound before you go make it hard.

HOW TO SCALE
Move up when you can run the whole rep without a reset - land balanced enough to go again
immediately. Drop a level when you cannot, and drop it without arguing.
Levels are per DRILL. Sitting at L2 on one and L6 on another is the system working.
When a level moves, overwrite the NOW line next to that drill. That is the only tracking this needs.

pages.title: Good Shooting
pages.body:
GOOD SHOOTING
Compound drills. No make standards. Scale by LEVEL. Write your level next to each drill.
Two Good Handles drills come first, before this page. Some drills here also enter through
handling - see the entries menu below.

HANDLING ENTRIES - the menu. Any drill below can be entered through one of these.
Higher levels on every ladder call for one. This is where handling in awkward situations and
sharpening moves live now - they are how you ARRIVE, not a separate workout.
  CHASE IT       throw it ahead off the wall or a hard roll, sprint it down, pick it up moving
  SCRAMBLE UP    start on the floor with the ball already bouncing, get to your feet, go
  OUT OF THE BOX two chairs a body width apart, work it low and fast, explode out
  TWO BALL DROP  two going, drop one, immediately go with the other
  OFF A COUNTER  killer cross to burnsey, in and out to spin, reverse through to euro,
                 misdirection through and behind, lowmans
THE SHARPNESS TEST: did the move take you somewhere? Alone, a move that ends where it started
was decoration. Ground covered is the measure.

YOUR FIVE TARGETS AND WHERE THEY GET HIT
                          balance | release speed | perception | deeper | awkward pickup
Spin Spin Back Pull Up      core        some          some        opt         -
Roll And Pick Up            core         some         core        opt        core
Lose The Rim                some        core          core        opt         -
Sprint Into It              core        some          some        opt         some
Skater Stepback             core        some           -          opt         -
Deep Work                    -           -             -         core         -
Two or three drills a session. Deep Work runs short and on its own - see why below.

1. SPIN SPIN BACK PULL UP                                     NOW: L___
Spin start, spin back, straight into a 1-dribble pull up. You leave the spin still rotating, have
to kill the rotation, and the rim was behind you a half second ago.
  L1  One spin, 1 dribble pull up, midrange
  L2  Add the spin back
  L3  From three
  L4  Both directions
  L5  Fadeaway instead of the pull up
  L6  The shot is called as you come out of the second spin
  L7  One count - pickup to release inside a second
  L8  Enter it off a handling entry - chase it, scramble up, or out of the box
  L9  Run it tired, end of the block

2. ROLL AND PICK UP                                           NOW: L___
Roll it out, chase it down, pick it up, shoot from wherever you got it. Worst starting position
you own, and you never get to pre-set your feet for a spot you chose.
  L1  Slow roll, strong side, midrange
  L2  Faster roll
  L3  Roll it to your weak side
  L4  Pick it up moving backwards
  L5  Bad bounce off the wall instead of a roll
  L6  Shoot from exactly where it stopped - no stepping into a spot you like
  L7  One count from the pickup
  L8  From three
  L9  Enter it off a handling entry

3. LOSE THE RIM                                               NOW: L___
High bounce at half, back pedal, 180, no dip. You lose the rim and have to re-find it late,
and the no-dip means you cannot buy time on the way up.
  L1  Back pedal, 180, normal gather
  L2  No dip
  L3  Back pedal further
  L4  Turn later
  L5  Self-toss off the backboard behind you - you never see it until you turn
  L6  Call a number off the wall before you release
  L7  One count
  L8  From three, then a step deeper
  L9  Enter it off a handling entry

4. SPRINT INTO IT                                             NOW: L___
High bounce, touch the paint, sprint into a curl, shoot on arrival with your feet still going.
  L1  Jog into the curl
  L2  Full sprint
  L3  Release before the feet fully set
  L4  Curl then relocate - two moves before the shot
  L5  The spot is called while you are sprinting
  L6  One count
  L7  From three
  L8  Enter it off a handling entry
  L9  After conditioning

5. SKATER STEPBACK                                            NOW: L___
Force production off a leg already travelling sideways.
  L1  Skater stepback, midrange
  L2  From three
  L3  Wider skater
  L4  Both ways
  L5  Skater into a stepback the OTHER way
  L6  One count
  L7  Off a live pickup
  L8  Enter it off a handling entry

DEEP WORK - short, on its own, form first                     NOW: L___
This one does not compound. Range needs a clean release and stacking constraints on it teaches
you to heave. Keep it to a few minutes at the end.
  L1  One-hand form shots at the arc, each hand
  L2  Two feet behind the arc, normal mechanics
  L3  Four feet behind
  L4  From the logo
  THE RULE: range comes from your legs and a cleaner release, never from throwing harder. If a
  shot needs an extra dip, a hitch, or a heave, you are too deep - come back a step. Add distance
  only when the release looks identical to your free throw.

HOW TO SCALE
Move up when you can run the rep without a reset. Drop a level when you cannot, without arguing.
Levels are per drill. When one moves, overwrite the NOW line next to that drill.

pages.title: Good Handling
pages.body:
GOOD HANDLING
Compound drills. No make standards. Scale by LEVEL.
TWO OF THESE START EVERY MORNING, after Vitamins and before Good Shooting or Good Finishing.
Rotate which two. Over a week all five get run.
Every rep on this page ends in a MOVE THAT GOES SOMEWHERE, at speed, out of a position you did
not want to be in. If a rep ends in a dribble, it did not count.

YOUR THREE TARGETS AND WHERE THEY GET HIT
                        speed | awkward | sharpening
Chase And Counter        core     core       core
Scramble To Attack       core     core       some
Tight To Open            core     core       core
Two Ball Breakout        core     some       some
Two or three a session.

THE MOVE MENU - every drill below finishes into one of these
Killer cross to burnsey | In and out to spin layup | Reverse through to euro |
Misdirection through and behind | Lowmans
The drills are the delivery. These are the content. Rotate which one you feed in.

1. CHASE AND COUNTER                                          NOW: L___
Throw it ahead, sprint it down, pick it up on the move, straight into a move, finish.
You never get a clean pickup and you never get to set your feet before the move.
  L1  Roll it ahead, jog, pick up, one move, finish
  L2  Full sprint
  L3  Pick it up with the weak hand
  L4  Pick it up moving AWAY from the rim, turn into the move
  L5  Bad bounce off the wall instead of a roll
  L6  The move is called as you pick it up
  L7  Chairs where you pick up, so the move has to be tight
  L8  Tired, end of the block

2. SCRAMBLE TO ATTACK                                         NOW: L___
Start on the floor with the ball already bouncing. Get up, go, move, finish.
The ball is never dead. If you have to pick it up off the floor to stand, the rep is over.
  L1  Kneeling, get up, one move, finish
  L2  Seated
  L3  Prone, dive to your feet
  L4  Full speed out of it
  L5  The move is called as you rise
  L6  Weak hand only the whole way
  L7  Chair to beat immediately out of the stand-up

3. TIGHT TO OPEN                                              NOW: L___
Two chairs a body width apart. Work the ball inside the box, low and fast, then explode out
into a move that covers ground.
The box trains the handle. The exit trains the move. It is one rep, not two.
  L1  Series in the box, then a move out
  L2  Narrower box
  L3  Knee height the whole time inside
  L4  Timed inside - 15s of work before the exit
  L5  Exit blind - eyes on a target across the gym, not on the box
  L6  Eyes on a target across the gym the whole time
  L7  Exit to your weak side every rep
  L8  Exit side called late

4. TWO BALL BREAKOUT                                          NOW: L___
Two balls going. Drop one on your own cue, immediately into a move at speed with the other.
Your hands are busy, so the move has to come out without you setting it up.
  L1  Stationary, drop one, one move
  L2  Opposite rhythm before the drop
  L3  On the move before the drop
  L4  Which ball you keep is called late
  L5  Full sprint out of it into the finish

HOW TO SCALE
Move up when you can run the rep without losing the ball AND the move still covers ground.
If you never nearly lose it, the level is too low.
THE TEST FOR SHARPNESS: did the move actually take you somewhere? Alone, with nobody to beat, a
move that ends where it started was decoration. Ground covered is the whole measure.
When a level moves, overwrite the NOW line next to that drill.

pages.title: Passing
pages.body:
PASSING
10-15 min, four times a week - Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Afternoon.
Two things only: can you hit a target, and do you know which one.
Not a Good drill, but the same idea - you should be off balance and moving fast when the ball
leaves your hand. A pass thrown from a good position is not the pass you need to practice.

THE TARGETS - three, on a wall
LEFT | MIDDLE | RIGHT
Tape or chalk. Keep them SMALL - a target you can hit from anywhere is not a target.
The wall is the point: it rebounds instantly, it needs no setup, and it is always available.

THE SHAPE OF EVERY REP
1. An entry that makes you fast, off balance, or both
2. Split Second calls the target while you are already moving
3. Hit it, with the pass the round is on

ENTRIES - pick one per round, rotate them
Live dribble at speed
Off a jump stop
Off the wrong foot
Out of a spin
Drifting or falling away from the wall
Off a loose-ball pickup

PASSES - the ROUND names the pass, the CALL names the target
Pocket | Hook | One-hand push | Skip | Drop-off | Wrap | Lob
Change the pass every round so the same three targets get hit six different ways across the week.

THE APP
Split Second, Passing section. Three calls - Left, Middle, Right - and all three are baked audio,
so they come through a Bluetooth speaker like the beeps do.
It asks how many you hit at the end of the set. That number is the whole record.

LEVEL                                                        NOW: L___
  L1  Stationary, target known before you start
  L2  Off a live dribble, target known
  L3  Split Second calls it - the call lands as you gather
  L4  Full speed
  L5  Off-balance entries only
  L6  Releasing as you move AWAY from the wall
  L7  Weak hand
  L8  Call names the target AND the pass
  L9  Two stacked - off balance at full speed, weak hand

THE STANDARD
Hit the target. A pass that misses it is a turnover with extra steps.
Eyes to the target LAST. Stare it down the whole way and the rep does not count.
Every pass off a live dribble or a gather. Never from a standstill above L1.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT NEED
Live reps. You pass more than you shoot at practice and so does everyone - the live half takes
care of itself. This block exists for accuracy under stress and for the decision, nothing else.

pages.title: READS - The Daily Block
pages.body:
READS - THE DAILY BLOCK
Every action, every read, every day. Afternoon.
Good drills make the skill hard. Reps make it automatic. Neither one makes you decide, because
every rep in both is a move you picked before you started. This is the block where you do not
know the answer when you begin the rep.

HOW IT RUNS
Run every section, every day. You set the reps per section - 20 to 30 is the working range, and
some sections deserve more than others. Split Second calls it, you execute.
The setup changes between sections - cone as the screener, chair at the slot, spot beyond the arc.
Reset it and keep moving. The changeover is not rest.

THE SCORE
Makes out of the reps you set. One number per section, entered in the app the moment the set ends.
A rep is a make when you did what the call said AND finished it.
Right read, missed finish is not a make. Wrong read that happens to go in is not a make either.

HOW IT GETS HARDER - the call comes later, the shot does not get harder
                                                             NOW: L___
L1  Three or four calls live. The call lands during the countdown.
L2  The full call set live. More options to choose between is a harder read at the same reps.
L3  The call lands late - at the screen, at the catch, at the gather.
L4  Execute window tightened. 4s, then 3s, then 2s.
L5  NOT BUILT YET - two actions chained, the second call coming off the first. This needs app
    work and is on the list. Do not wait on it to run L1 through L4.

MOVING UP
Beat your number twice at a level, then move up. The app flags it when you have.
Levels are per SECTION, not per page. Ice sitting at L4 while Closeout sits at L2 is the system
working, not the system failing.

THE SECTIONS - the whole list runs, every day
Ball screen coverages   Drop | Switch-Hedge | Ice | DHO
Everything else         Closeout | Float and Drop Reads | Fade
The skill sections      Finishing | Catch and Shoot
HANDLING IS GONE FROM THE APP, not just off the list - the section and its audio were removed on
8/31. Four of its seven calls were warmup drill names - Burnsey, Lowman, Reverse through,
Misdirection - which got read as game moves and you corrected. It comes back when you dictate the
moves you would actually use to beat somebody off the dribble.

WHY THE CALL IS REALISTIC
You can see the coverage - the defense calls it out loud as you come into the screen. Knowing it
before the rep is not a cheat, it is the game. What the app is standing in for is the part you
cannot know: what the defenders actually do inside the coverage, since they cannot plug every hole.

DEFENSE READS
The defense sections run in the defense block, not here. See the Defense page in Court movement.

pages.title: ON THE MOVE - The Shooting Block
pages.body:
ON THE MOVE - THE SHOOTING BLOCK
Eight ways you arrive. Six shots off every one of them.
This absorbed Bag Shooting on 8/31 - its back pedal, its deep slides and its shot fake pull-up
moved here, and everything else on that page was already a duplicate of this one.

THE EIGHT MOVEMENTS - two fixed halves, alternate them
HALF A - off a screen
  Fade          off the screen
  Curl          off the screen
  Zip up        off an elevator or a pin
  Deep slides   off an off-ball screen
HALF B - no screen, you get there on your own
  Drift         to the corner
  Lift          to the wing
  Transition    full sprint
  Back pedal    lose the rim and re-find it late

THE SIX SHOTS - every movement runs all six
1  Catch and shoot
2  No dip
3  Jab, step back, shoot
4  Shot fake, sidestep, shoot
5  Shot fake, pull up
6  Jab, shoot

WHY IT IS IN HALVES
Eight movements times six shots is forty eight combinations, and at two attempts each that is
ninety six shots standing in one block. Half is forty eight, which is a block you will actually
finish instead of abandoning at combination thirty.
Each half carries its OWN bar, so your number is always compared against the same work. Alternate
them and both halves get run across the week.

HOW IT RUNS
One half a session. Four movements, six shots, two attempts each. Forty eight shots.
Two passes, not one block - take your two, go to the next combination, come back around for the
second pass. Same rule as every reps page.
Vary the rep inside the combination: which side, how hard you come off, exactly where you catch
it. The combination is fixed. The rep is not.

FIX YOUR DISTANCE - write it in and do not move it
The number only means something if the shot is the same shot every time. 34/48 taken a step inside
the arc and 34/48 from three are not the same day, the same way corners and the top are not the
same fifty on 50/50.
Fade ___   Curl ___   Zip ___   Deep slides ___
Drift ___  Lift ___   Transition ___   Back pedal ___

THE SCORE
Makes out of 48, counted per half.
HALF A BAR:  ___ / 48
HALF B BAR:  ___ / 48

SETTING THE BARS THE FIRST TIME
You do not know your numbers yet, and a bar I guessed at would be wrong in one direction or the
other. Run each half twice as written, then set that half's bar off your own two numbers. Same way
50/50 gets its line - from you, not from me.

MOVING A BAR
Clear it twice in a row, or clear it by three in a single day, and that bar goes up one.
Miss it twice in a row and it goes down one.
Two clearances and not one, on purpose: at forty eight shots a single make is two percent, and a
bar that moves on one good day is a bar that moves on luck.

WHEN A BAR GETS HIGH - raise the setting, reset that bar
Clearing comfortably means the shots got easy, not that you are finished. Move ONE setting up and
start that bar again, lower, at the new difficulty.
  SETTING 1  Controlled speed into the catch. Feet set before you rise.
  SETTING 2  Full speed into every movement.
  SETTING 3  Release on arrival - feet still going, no gather you did not earn.
  SETTING 4  Run it at the end of the block, tired.
HALF A SETTING: ___     HALF B SETTING: ___
The two halves do not have to be on the same setting.

STILL UNDEFINED - one line is yours
"Deep slides off an off-ball screen" has never been defined. Until you say what the movement is,
run it as a long lateral slide into the catch. Say the word and it goes on the line.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not a Good drill. Nothing is stacked on top of the shot and there is no level ladder on the shot
itself. The job is your footwork and your body feeling right on the move, and the percentage
climbing because of it. Awkward is the morning's job and it stays there.

pages.title: DRIBBLE BAG
pages.body:
DRIBBLE BAG
Everything you score with below the arc off your own dribble. Bag Off Dribble and Bag once by
folded into one page on 8/31. Every line came across exactly as it was, standards untouched.

Run it varied, in two passes. Never take the same rep twice - before every attempt change the
spot, the entry, the tempo, the depth or the angle. Take 2 attempts, move to the next drill,
come back for the other 2 on a second pass.

HALF A - OFF THE DRIBBLE, MIDRANGE          9 drills, 17 sides
Mistiming pull up - 5/7
Drop hezi pull, volleyball line - 3/4 ea way
Top of key sprint to corner - 3/4 ea way
Full sprint into stop, transition - 3/4 ea way
Full sprint hard stop step back, transition - 3/4 ea way
Drop through step back - 3/4 ea way
Drop through cross hang - 3/4 ea way
Drop misdirection through - 3/4 ea way
McGarrity - 3/4 ea way

HALF B - ONCE BY, PAINT AND SHORT           12 drills, 24 sides
Middle pullups off drop - 3/4 ea side
Drew Hanlan bump out - 3/4 ea side
Block stop hook layup - 2/2 ea side
Block stop, shot fake, pivot fadeaway - 3/4 ea side
Block stop, pivot, shot fake, step through - 3/4 ea side
Middle stop bump fade - 3/4 ea side
Middle stop bump, soft float over the front rim - 3/4 ea side
Middle stop, shot fake, pivot fadeaway - 3/4 ea side
Barkley Kobe spin back - 3/4 ea side
Barkley middle bump hook - 3/4 ea side
Barkley middle fadeaway - 3/4 ea side
Barkley baseline fadeaway - 3/4 ea side

NOTES CARRIED OVER
Mistiming pull up is the one high-volume rhythm drill and keeps 5/7 as written, no side counter.
"Full sprint into stop, transition" here is the OFF-DRIBBLE version. The CATCH version is
"Transition" on ON THE MOVE - The Shooting Block. Two different drills, same words.
Block stop hook layup sits at 2/2 because it is a rim finish and your own bar for rim finishes is
"2/2 or it doesnt count". Say the word and it goes back to 3/4.
Four of Half B's twelve are fadeaways, which makes it your most-repped shot family in the program
and also your lowest-value shot. Not changing it - worth knowing.

THE SIZE OF THIS PAGE
41 sides at 3 or 4 attempts each is around 150 attempts if you run the whole thing in one session.
It is written in halves for that reason. Alternate them the way On The Move alternates, or run it
whole on fewer days - your call, and the page works either way.

pages.title: 50/50 - The Standard
pages.body:
50/50 - THE STANDARD
Read this once. It turns the one number you already produce every day into a real one.

WHEN
End of the afternoon block, both halves, back to back. Shooting them tired is the better rep and
it means you log the whole day in one moment instead of carrying a number around since morning.

THE 50 THREES - 5 racks of 10, always these spots, always this order
1. Right corner - 10
2. Right wing - 10
3. Top of the key - 10
4. Left wing - 10
5. Left corner - 10
Type each rack the second it ends. Five small numbers beat one number at the end.
WHY THIS MATTERS: without fixed spots, 34/50 from the corners and 34/50 from the top look identical
in your log and they are not the same day. Undefined spots are why the number never meant anything.

THE 50 FREE THROWS - 5 sets of 10
Sets of 10 only so you never have to hold a count past ten.

LOG IT
One row in the Log table: date, threes out of 50, free throws out of 50.
78 rows exist and at six days a week they run out in mid-November. Add more before the season.

WHAT A GOOD DAY IS
You do not know yet, and that is the point. Shoot it for ten days, then your line gets set from
your own numbers rather than from a guess. Until then the only job is putting a row in the table.

pages.title: Compete + Fatigue
pages.body:
COMPETE + FATIGUE
Attach this to the END of your bag work, twice a week. It is a finisher, not a session.
Games are played tired. Every other skill block in your program is done fresh.
Pick one and rotate. About 10 minutes.

1. MAKE OR REPEAT
Pick a bag package. You do not leave a drill until you hit its written standard.
Miss the standard and the whole drill runs again. No partial credit.

2. SHOOTING ON EMPTY
Sprint the floor twice, then shoot 5 from the wing. Five rounds.
Track makes out of 25. This is the honest number, not your fresh one.

3. FREE THROWS TIRED
Every time you finish a hard block anywhere in your day, shoot 2 free throws before you sit down.
Log makes out of the day's total attempts.

4. BEAT THE CLOCK
Shot clock on your phone. 30 seconds to get a specific shot off a specific action.
10 rounds. Do not get the shot off and it counts as a miss.

5. ONE MINUTE SPOTS
60 seconds at one spot, as many makes as you can. Rest 60. Five spots.
Log total makes and compare month to month.

LOG IT - here, overwrite it each time
LAST RUN: drill ___   number ___   date ___
The number here will always be worse than your fresh number. That is the point.
When the gap between tired and fresh shrinks, you are actually getting somewhere.

pages.title: Partner Menu
pages.body:
PARTNER MENU
Grab one of these when somebody is in the gym with you. 20 minutes, zero planning.
This REPLACES the passing block that day. Live reads beat wall reps every time.
Pick by what you have not done recently, not by what you feel like doing.

1. LIVE PASSING READS - 20 min
He plays help off your drive. He commits or he does not and you read it.
Drive and read 6x ea side, then ball screen with him as the coverage 10x ea side.
The only rule: he never tells you what he is doing beforehand.

2. ONE ON ONE, FULL - 20 min
Live, both ends. First to 7, win by 2. Write the score down.
Pick what you are hunting before you start, same as a practice intention.

3. CLOSEOUT AND CONTAIN, LIVE - 20 min
He starts with the ball on the wing, you start under the rim. You close, he attacks.
6 reps then switch. You win the rep if he never gets a straight-line drive.

4. SCREEN NAVIGATION, LIVE - 20 min
He comes off a screen you have to get through. Over, under, or top lock - call it before the rep.
8 reps ea side then switch.

5. CONTESTED SHOOTING - 20 min
He closes out for real, you shoot for real. 20 off the catch, 20 off the dribble.
Track makes. Compare it to your 50/50 number - the gap is what pressure costs you.

6. REBOUNDING AND BOX OUT - 20 min
Live box out off a shot. First to 10 rebounds.
The most under-trained thing a guard can do with a partner.

LOG IT - here, overwrite it each time
LAST RUN: drill ___   score ___   date ___
If you have not run one of these in three weeks, that is the one you do next.

pages.title: Practice Intentions
pages.body:
PRACTICE INTENTIONS
Live reps without a target are just cardio. Pick ONE before every practice and every run.
One. Not three. You cannot hunt three things at once and you will end up hunting none.
Write it on the line below before you go, and score yourself out of 10 after.
TODAY: ___                                 AFTER: ___ /10
LAST PRACTICE: ___                         ___ /10

DEFENSE
I do not get beat baseline once.
I get over every ball screen. No going under unless I call it first.
I am in a stance before he catches, not after.
I finish possessions - I box out every single time a shot goes up.
I talk on every screen. Every one.

PASSING AND DECISIONS
I hit the roller at least three times.
I make the extra pass every time I am two feet from a good shot and someone has a better one.
Zero live-dribble turnovers.
I look weak side before I pick up my dribble.
I throw at least one skip pass.

SCORING
I get to a left-hand finish twice.
No contested twos.
I shoot every open catch-and-shoot without hesitating.
I get downhill off the first side action instead of the third.

MOVEMENT AND COMPETE
I sprint the floor both ways every possession of one full drill.
My hips stay low through every screen I navigate.
I stop on one step, not three.

HOW TO USE IT
Rotate through them. Do not repeat one until you have scored yourself 8 or better on it twice.
A 4 out of 10 is more useful than a 9 - it tells you what to hunt next time.
The point is not the score. The point is that you walked in looking for something.

pages.title: NERVOUS SYSTEM - Hot and Cold
pages.body:
NERVOUS SYSTEM - HOT AND COLD
The mental side. Not reads, not IQ. The piece that decides whether the skills you built show up.
Written after the first practice with the new team: nervous walking in, mistakes compounding,
playing to not mess up, body gone weak. Hot first, then cold. This page is the tool for both.
Nothing here is scored, levelled or laddered. Confidence is not a drill. It is what evidence
leaves behind, and the only job of this page is to keep you doing things that produce evidence.

THE LOOP - why it went the way it went
Nerves put the body in a threat state. Under threat the body protects, it does not perform.
That is the weakness you felt.
With nothing specific to hunt, "don't mess up" filled the empty slot.
Avoidance goals make you slow, because every option gets risk-checked before you act.
Slow is what produces the mistakes. Each one confirms the threat. Round it goes.
The fix is not feeling more confident. It is: bring the body down a notch, fill the slot, and
cut the loop after every mistake so nothing compounds. Three tools, one each.

THE TWO BREATHS - opposite jobs, do not mix them up
DOWN  Two inhales through the nose - a full one, then a short top-up on top of it - then one long
      slow exhale through the mouth until you are empty. One of these drops arousal faster than
      anything else you can do on purpose. In a practice or a game, one to three. Five minutes of
      it is the morning practice.
UP    Short sharp inhales through the nose, quick exhale, and MOVE - sprint, jump, slap the floor.
      For when you have gone flat. It is the opposite tool.

DAILY - trains the reflex so it is there when you need it. No new time.
MORNING  Your "Meditate 5 minutes" slot. Five minutes of DOWN breaths, one after another, sitting
         up, eyes closed. That is the whole practice. You are grooving the exact breath you will
         use walking into the gym, so it works without thinking when your hands are shaking.
NIGHT    Your "Slow Breathe" line. In through the nose 4 seconds, out through the nose 6, five
         minutes, lying down. Longer out than in - that is the only rule.
GYM      The reset below runs after every miss in 50/50 and every wrong read in Reads. Dozens of
         free reps a day of the thing that stops mistakes compounding, in a place where a miss
         costs nothing.

BEFORE - walking in
The target is not calm. Calm is flat and flat gets beat. The target is ready without threat:
same heart rate, no danger in it.
1. Three DOWN breaths on the walk in. Takes the top off. Does not take you to zero.
2. Say the intention out loud. ONE, off the Practice Intentions page, chosen before you left the
   room. Now the slot is full and "don't mess up" has nowhere to sit.
3. First possession is an effort job - sprint the floor, hit somebody on a screen, talk. Something
   you cannot fail. You are in the practice before the ball has touched your hands.
Nerves and excitement are the same body. The only difference is the label you put on it. When you
feel it: "that is the body getting ready". Never "calm down" - it does not work, and it tells
you something is wrong.

BETWEEN - the reset, after every mistake, 3 seconds
Mistakes are not the problem. Carrying one into the next possession is.
The reset is physical so it does not need a thought you might not have in you:
  1. One physical cue. Wipe your hands on your shorts, or pull the jersey. Same one every time.
  2. One DOWN breath.
  3. Eyes up to the next thing - the ball, or your man's chest. Find your job.
Done. You do not review the mistake. You do not get to review it until film.
Same reset after a good play. A good play you are still thinking about is the next mistake.
This is what you groove in the gym. By the time it matters it is not a decision, it is a habit.

GONE COLD - the opposite of everything above
You will know it: passing up open shots, body heavy, hoping the play goes somewhere else. That is
the freeze branch. Slow breathing sinks you further. Do not use it here.
1. UP breaths. Two or three sharp ones, and move - sprint to your spot on the next dead ball.
2. Eyes OUT. At the rim, at his chest, at the ball. Not inward. Cold lives inside your head.
3. Voice. Call every screen, every switch, every get-back, loud. Talking is a job you cannot
   fail and it drags your attention back onto the game.
4. One effort goal for the next three possessions that skill cannot ruin: sprint both ways, box
   out every shot, get a deflection. Effort still works when skill is gone, and every one you
   finish is a piece of evidence. Evidence is the only thing confidence is made of.
An open shot is still shot. Hesitating on it is the symptom, not a fix. Shoot it and reset.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not a confidence ladder. Not a mood score. Not a page you level up. The only measure is whether
the tools got used, and that is yes or no.
LAST PRACTICE: walked in with the slot full? ___   reset after mistakes? ___   went cold? ___

WHEN IT IS BIGGER THAN A PAGE
If it gets to where it got - the panic, the body shutting down - and it happens again, that is a
recurring thing worth taking to somebody. CWRU counselling is free and a sports psych is standard
equipment at the level you are chasing. It is a tool, same as a lift.

pages.title: Film + IQ
pages.body:
FILM + IQ
10 minutes, off court, in the evening. Costs you no gym time at all.
This is the cheapest development available to you and the one almost every player skips.
Rotation: A, B, C, D. Check the LAST RUN line.
LAST RUN: ___ (A, B, C or D)   date ___

BLOCK A - YOUR OWN GAME FILM - 10 min
Watch your own possessions from practice or a run, whatever you can get.
Count three things and write the numbers here: live-dribble turnovers, times a better pass was
open and you shot instead, and times you got beat off the dribble.
LAST COUNT: turnovers ___   passed-up ___   beaten ___
Do not watch for highlights. You already know what your good plays looked like.

BLOCK B - READ THE COVERAGE - 10 min
Pull up any college or NBA game. Watch nothing but ball screens.
Before the ball handler acts, PAUSE and call it out loud: over, under, switch, drop, hedge.
Then play it and see what the defense actually did and what he did about it.
20 reps. You are training the read, not the move.

BLOCK C - STUDY A GUARD - 10 min
Pick one guard built like you who plays your role. Watch one game a week of him and only him.
Watch what he does WITHOUT the ball and how he gets the ball where he wants it.
Steal one specific thing, write it down, take it into the gym that week.

BLOCK D - YOUR TEAM'S ACTIONS - 10 min
Know your own playbook cold. Every action, every counter, every spot you occupy.
The fastest way onto the floor as a freshman is being the guy who never blows the play.
Write out one action from memory. If you cannot, that is the one you study tomorrow.

FILM CHECK
Once the movement analysis is built, Block A becomes the slot where your own movement clips get
reviewed alongside your game possessions. Capture per the Film Protocol page in Court movement.

PROGRESSION
Overwrite the LAST RUN line. Streak beats depth here - ten minutes four times a week beats an hour once.
Block A: those three numbers should trend down over a month. That is the entire measure.
Block B: progress by calling the read EARLIER - before the screen is set instead of after.

pages.title: PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS
pages.body:
PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS

Read this before practice. Pick two. Not five, two. Score yourself out of 10 after, on the line below.
PICKED: ___ and ___          AFTER: ___ /10 and ___ /10

This page exists because these are the things that cannot be repped alone. Reps Transition grooves the movement. This is where the deciding gets trained, and Tuesday is the only day it can happen.

TRANSITION OFFENSE
First look is up the floor on every rebound and every make, before the ball goes down. Count the possessions I looked first.
Push past the free throw line before I decide anything. No decision made above the arc.
Name the advantage to myself every break. Numbers, mismatch, or none. If none, pull it out on the first beat instead of driving into a set defense.
Every break ends one of three ways. I finish it, I hit the man ahead, or I pull it out clean. No dead dribble in the middle third.
When I am not the ball, I run wide to the corner every time. No drifting to the wing early.
As the trail man I am ready before the catch, and I shoot it in one motion if it is there.

TRANSITION DEFENSE
Paint first, man second. Get to the paint, then find who I have.
I take the most dangerous man, not my man, until we are matched up.
I talk on every get back. Call the ball, call who I have, out loud, every possession.
My first step after my own shot is back. Count the possessions I lost that step.

READING A CLOSEOUT
Three options on the catch and I decide on the catch, not before it. Shoot it. Attack the high shoulder. One more, and relocate.

BALL SCREEN, THE LATE READ
I do not decide before I leave. I read the coverage after the first dribble, not at the point of the screen. If I know the answer before I come off it, that was a bag rep, not a live one.
Hedge and blitz are the two coverages I have never repped anywhere. Those are the ones to go looking for at practice.

pages.title: GROUP WORKOUT IDEAS - parked
pages.body:
GROUP WORKOUT IDEAS - PARKED
Everything that needs a body. Nothing here is scheduled. We look at this after the solo system
is finished.

WHY THIS PAGE EXISTS
Contact and physicality came out of every solo page on purpose. A wall does not move, does not
recover, and does not push back - training contact against one teaches you to lean, not to move
somebody. All of it lives here until there is a person on the other side of it.

CONTACT - pulled out of the solo pages
Finish through a bump. Take the hit on the way up and let it change nothing about the finish.
Attack into contact, absorb it, counter off it into the finish. The counter is the point.
Navigate a screen with a real body in it - get skinny, take the hit, keep the line.
Hold your line while somebody rides your hip. Keep the path and keep the height.
Play through a bump on the catch before you shoot.
Post-up and seal work - anything where you move a body off a spot.

DEFENSE THAT NEEDS A PERSON
Deny work. You said you are open to this in a group.
Live one on one, full court and half court. The real version of everything on the Defense page.
Guarding a real screen where the screener actually screens.
Help and recover with a second offensive player who punishes a late closeout.
Post defense and guarding up a size.

PASSING AND READS THAT NEED A PERSON
Live-dribble passing where the help defender actually commits, so the read is real.
Two on one and three on two - the decision, not the delivery.
Off-ball cutting and screening timing, where arriving early or late actually costs something.

WHAT A PARTNER IS WORTH MOST FOR
Not more reps. Reps you can get alone. A partner is worth the things that cannot be faked:
a defender who reacts, contact that moves you, and a passer whose timing is not your own.
Spend partner time on those and nothing else.
